supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42:51 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-ZADAMS-01 as ian.doyle, using the exact \FILE-SUN-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1 path described in the supplied IT practices. Its command line included -ExecutionPolicy Bypass.
A network logon for ian.doyle to WS-ZADAMS-01 was recorded from source address 10.55.10.23 shortly before the PowerShell launch.
The PowerShell process made a proxy connection that transferred 38,800,251 response bytes, and created a temporary file under ian.doyle's profile.
PowerShell launched wusa.exe to install windows11-kb5047001-x64.msu quietly without restarting, consistent with the supplied description of IT workstation patching.
The observed PowerShell process exited about 42 seconds after it started.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not show the contents or integrity of Patch-Workstations.ps1, the downloaded or transferred payload, or the temporary file.
The proxy connection record provides byte counts but not the requested URL or response content.
The records show the PowerShell command, account, and nearby network logon, but do not independently establish who initiated the remote action or its authorization.
claims_not_established: The logs do not establish that the script or patch package was unmodified and authentic.
The logs do not establish the identity of the person operating the source host for the ian.doyle logon.
The logs do not establish the exact contents of the proxy response or temporary file.
unrelated_findings: At 13:30 UTC, WS-IDOYLE-01 recorded a network logon for ian.doyle from 10.55.10.21; other records identify 10.55.10.21 as WS-ZADAMS-01. This is an unexpected direction relative to the supplied remote-administration practice and merits separate review; it does not by itself change the disposition of the observed patching activity.
